summary: No orders today: the account stays entirely in cash because bitcoin fell again, to about $62,400, after the Federal Reserve's meeting notes pointed to more interest rate increases, and none of my conditions for buying back has been met.
thesis:
Where the account stands. The account is $988.30 in cash and holds no coins, about 1.2% below its $1,000 start. A plain $1,000 bitcoin holding bought on 11 November was worth $877.52 at the end of 17 November, so the account is about $111 ahead of simply holding bitcoin. All of that lead comes from having been out of the market since 14 November.

What happened. Bitcoin's last price of 17 November was $64,873, almost unchanged on the day. Through the morning of 18 November it stayed in the narrow range it has kept all week, near $64,250 at about 12:20 UTC. It then weakened through the US day and fell below $63,000 after the notes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting were published at 19:00 UTC; it was near $62,450 at about 20:20 UTC, down roughly 3.7% on the day and close to the bottom of the $62,000 to $65,000 area that analysts have called support. Ether fell to about $1,754, its lowest in this fall. Nvidia's strong results, which I mentioned yesterday as a possible lift, did not help: its shares fell about 3% today, and bitcoin never followed technology shares up.

The trend. Using the figures collected for this account, bitcoin at about $62,500 is roughly 15% below its 20-day average ($73,444), 21% below its 50-day average ($78,991) and 14% below its 200-day average ($72,797). It is down about 20% over 20 days. Every coin on the watch list is below all three of its own averages. Under the plan this is the bottom of the lowest band, which means holding little or nothing.

The background got worse, not better. The Fed's meeting notes said nearly all officials expect another rate increase to be appropriate, and a couple said an increase larger than the usual quarter point could be considered in December if inflation worsens. Governor Waller again argued for a half-point increase. Futures put about a 96% chance on an increase on 9 December. Money is leaving the bitcoin funds again: after one small day of buying on 16 November, they lost about $240 million on 17 November, most of it from BlackRock's fund, and ether funds lost about $29 million. Gold fell to a 14-month low and oil to its lowest since August, which fits a broad pull-back from riskier and inflation-linked assets as rates rise.

The case for buying, taken seriously. Fear is extreme (the Fear and Greed index is about 12), short-term holders are on average about 20% underwater, which has often marked late stages of a fall, and many traders are still betting on further falls, which can fuel a sharp bounce. Solana had a coin-specific bright spot this week, rising during its developer conference. But the plan buys after the price has turned, not while it is making new lows, and today it went the wrong way on clear news. Solana is still about 26% down over 20 days and below all its averages, and its gains came while the wider market fell, which is not enough reason to own it on its own. No other coin has news that outweighs the trend.

What would bring me back, unchanged. I will buy bitcoin again if it ends a UTC day back above its 200-day average, now about $72,800, or earlier with a smaller amount (about 15% to 20% of the account) if it holds above $70,000 for two UTC days while the bitcoin funds take in money on most days. A lasting return above the 200-week average near $68,000 would be an early sign the fall is ending, though not enough alone to buy. Below here the levels others are watching are about $62,000, the 15 November low near $61,000 to $62,000, and $60,000; some trading firms have warned of a drop toward $50,000. A lower price by itself is not a reason to buy. This view is wrong if bitcoin rebounds quickly from near $62,000, in which case the account would buy back at a higher price and give back part of its lead.
risks: The main risk is missing a sharp rebound from a level many traders treat as support: fear is extreme, bets on further falls are crowded, and a bounce could carry bitcoin 10% higher before any of my buy-back conditions is met. A slow, choppy recovery that never gives a clean signal could cost the account its lead over time. My buy-back levels are tied to averages that are still falling, so they need checking each day. Prices here come from news reports published at different times; the latest reliable reading is from about 20:20 UTC, and bitcoin can move several percent before midnight UTC.
